text: Cypress isn’t just where I live-it’s home. I grew up in a very different Cypress, but while our city has grown, what makes it special hasn’t changed: strong families, opportunity, and community pride.

I attended local schools, played youth sports, and earned a degree in History and Business from Loyola Marymount. My career included consulting for a Fortune 5 financial firm and in education before I followed my passion and built a thriving dance studio. For 18 years, I’ve served Cypress families, led a dedicated team, managed a $1M + budget, and created an inclusive space for kids of all abilities—keeping people moving in the same direction, sometimes even on the beat.

I’ve served on the Cypress Senior Commission and volunteered in classrooms for a decade. As your current City Councilmember, I’ve worked with police and fire to keep Cypress safe, coordinated emergency relief for District 5 during the chemical spill, and developed mental health resources for kids, seniors, and veterans.

I’m focused on protecting local control, maintaining fiscal strength, and supporting smart, affordable housing solutions. I believe in investing in community space; great cities need places to gather, celebrate, and connect.
Let’s keep Cypress safe, strong, and full of opportunity.

text: Effective representation matters, especially on our City Council. For over 40 years, I served our communities as a firefighter, retiring as a Battalion Chief. Today I serve as an Emergency Manager for the County of Orange currently assigned to the Social Services Agency. My wife and I raised our family in District 5 for almost 30 years. We chose Cypress for simple reasons: great schools, safe streets, and a family-focused community.

I'm running because I understand how local government works and will stay Cypress focused guaranteeing that District 5 concerns are heard and addressed. I will ensure that our city returns to a financially frugal philosophy that placed us in the strong position we now enjoy.

As your councilman, I will make sure we build smartly, fighting major zoning changes that don't fit our neighborhoods. I will oppose plans to open Holder Street, disrupting our beloved walking path. I’ll work diligently on homeless concerns city wide, keeping our recreational areas safe.
When disaster hits, our best leaders rise. I've spent my career being ready for these moments: calm under pressure, focused on solutions, and always answering the call.
I hope to earn your vote.
